title: Workload Token Request
description: Request for a short-lived Baobab workload access token (ADR-0006 token profile, ADR-0007 workload identity). Provider-neutral (ADR-IAM-0019, ADR-IAM-0020, ADR-SHARED-017 SS14): it names the registered workload, the resource server it calls and the scopes it needs. It never carries a credential and never names a grant type, realm or other identity-provider construct. How the workload proves itself -- a federated platform-projected token exchanged as an RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant, private_key_jwt, or an IdP client credential -- follows the workload's credential_type in workload-registry.yaml and is presented through the implementing provider's own protocol binding, outside this contract. A federated_workload_token workload never holds a static secret.

workload_id.description: Canonical workload identifier: a key of workload-registry.yaml workloads. The provider refuses a workload that is not registered, not ACTIVE, or registered for another environment.

audience.description: Logical resource-server audience the token is for; must be one of the workload's allowed_audiences. A token for one audience does not work against another (ADR-0007 SS24-25).

scopes.description: Requested scopes from authorization/v1 scope-registry.yaml; each must be in the workload's allowed_scopes. Omitted means the workload's least-privilege default for the audience; never a wildcard.
